thread:
olivia: Heads up — staging CI started failing after I applied the keystore rotation. Lots of SAST alerts popped up for 'service-auth'. Anyone else seeing a spike?
sec-bot: Auto-scan complete: 23 findings in repo 'service-auth' (18 low, 3 medium, 2 high). Scan ID: scan-20260304-7070. Report: https://scans.internal/scan-20260304-7070 :eyes:
kevin: On it. Do we have any RBAC changes to the scanner service account in the last 24h?
leen: I rotated the keystore yesterday and updated the KMS IAM policy to the new key. I didn't intentionally touch the scanner SA binding, but I did run the keystore bootstrap which touched a few bindings.
jamal: Can you paste an example of a failing finding? sometimes rotation changes artifact paths and triggers false positives.
olivia: Pasting the top error and one finding:```
[ERROR] decrypt failed: AccessDenied: caller does not have permission to decrypt with keystore-key-v2
File: src/auth/session_store.go:42
Finding: insecure_temp_credential_assignment (medium) - assignment of temporary creds from environment variable
```
kevin: That decrypt error worries me — SAST flagged the code that reads env creds because our test harness falls back to reading plaintext env when KMS errors. If the decrypt step failed, the harness may be exercising fallback code paths that look like insecure usage.
leen: Good call. So this might be a pipeline/infra-induced FP rather than a real regression. Two poss: 1) scanner can't call KMS (RBAC) or 2) scanner pod can't reach keystore endpoint (network).
jamal: Quick checks: `kubectl get sa scanner -n ci -o yaml` and `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy keystore-key-v2 --project=infra-prod` — can someone run those?
olivia: Ran `kubectl get sa scanner -n ci -o yaml` — serviceAccount exists, tokenProjected: true. Not sure about IAM policy.
leen: I checked KMS policy: the binding to `serviceAccount:ci-scanner@infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com` was accidentally removed during rotation. Re-added now.
kevin: Nice find. Two action items: (A) re-run the CI scan once binding propagates, (B) add a pre-rotation checklist step to preserve scanner SA bindings. I'll also add a temporary detection to ignore SAST hits that arise when decrypt fails.
olivia: I'll open a ticket for the checklist and link to this thread. ticket: SEC-4321. Assigning to @leen for postmortem, and @kevin for rule suppression PR. :+1:
sec-bot: Detection note added to scan-20260304-7070: ignoring findings where `decrypt error` present in logs (temporary).
jamal: For auditability — can we backfill the KMS audit logs for the rotation window? Need to capture who/what removed binding.
leen: Yep. `gcloud logging read` is in progress, will attach results to SEC-4321. Initial view shows operator account `infra-ops@` ran the bootstrap script and an older script had a `removeBinding` step — likely accidental.
kevin: For immediate CI stability, I've opened PR #1812 that skips the fallback path in test harness and forces a mocked KMS response so SAST doesn't see plaintext flows. Will run tests after binding propagation.
olivia: Re-run kicked off — CI shows scan run in 3m.
sec-bot: Scan re-run complete: scan-20260304-7070-r2 — 4 findings now (all low). No medium/high.
kevin: Confirmed — root cause: RBAC binding removal caused KMS decrypt failures which exercised insecure fallback code paths, creating noisy SAST findings. Remediation: restored binding, PR #1812 to harden test harness, SEC-4321 for checklist + postmortem.
leen: Postmortem draft in SEC-4321 updated with audit logs and recommended guardrail: add a pre-rotation `verify-binding` step that checks expected SA bindings and aborts if diff detected.
jamal: Also recommend an alert if CI SAST results increase >10x after infra changes for 1h. Could be a signal of infra-induced noise.
olivia: Sounds good. Thanks all. Closing this thread once SEC-4321 has signoffs. :white_check_mark:
